resolutions.title: Redirection handling does not satisfy the declared operator closure
resolutions.action: Pushback: still applies — `git status >| out` split into a segment `out`, `<>` and `<&` were kept as arguments, and a here-document's body lines were read as commands. Repaired within the closure the spec declares: `>|`, `<>`, `<&` and a file-descriptor digit before any redirection are dropped with their target (a `>|` target named `git` is no segment), and an unquoted `<<` or `<<-` is refused at its opening line, so no fence holding a here-document can pass. Body consumption was not built: the extractor does not delimit the body, and the refusal row says so. Measured first: no here-document or rare redirection on today's surface. The spec's redirection row, a new here-document row and the closure sentence, design D1 and the proposal say so; tokenizer cases cover each form, the earlier `<<` case moved from dropped to refused.

retired: a digit before `>`, `>&`) and its target are dropped

introduced.text: if (line.startsWith('<<', i)) return { ok: false, refused: '<<' };
so no fence holding one passes the sweep (system walk, external W2)

final_assessment: System walk of the external half (2 findings): the capture-forms finding converged with the fresh half's and is stale here, resolved in the fresh log; the redirection closure is repaired — the rest of POSIX XCU 2.10's redirections are dropped with their targets and a here-document is refused at its opening line. 3286 tests green.
